move.why: The start design leaves every elementwise op and softmax on the CPU, which likely dominates the 93846 s. This step moves the per-layer norm, RoPE, activation, residual and attention ops to the vector unit, softmax to the star unit, and lm_head to the crossbar, with moderate VFU and star scaling. It tests whether offloading these ops cuts time enough to justify the area and effort.

Design #2 barely improved on the start, so the remaining cost is likely in attention and the vector-unit bandwidth/throughput limits. Moving attention onto the crossbars (the only option that avoids the KV-memory bandwidth bottleneck) while raising vfu bandwidth, lanes and star units tests whether attention is the dominant cost; the xbar value is now given as the bare option name, which fixes the rejected format.

Design #3 and #4 tie at 540.2 s, so extra VFU lanes are not the bottleneck. I'll start from #3 (embed and sample stay on cpu, so the rejected offloads are avoided) and raise the KV-memory bandwidth to 1 TB/s and switch to the transpose crossbar, which makes K appends single row writes. Together these target the KV traffic and attention path, which is the likely remaining cost.

Going from 64 to 256 vector lanes left the time unchanged (#3 vs #4), so vector throughput is not the bottleneck and the remaining cost is likely CPU-coprocessor transfers. Moving the link from cxl to package is the cheapest untested knob that targets that overhead on the best design so far (#5).
